messages:
Kevin (Support): heads-up — SilverMast just opened a ticket: embeddings p99 jumped from ~220ms to 2.8s around 09:10 UTC. customer says product-facing search is timing out. :rotating_light:
Oncall Bot: alert: silvermast-embeds-p99 spike detected — rolling 5m p99 = 2830ms, error rate +0.4% — linked incident ID #INC-1159
Jenna (Customer Success): attaching customer trace: they see timeouts on /v1/embeddings with key customer-sls-01. They pasted a snippet: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -d '{"input": "foo"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings` and it hangs >3s.
Alex (Oncall): thanks — I'm taking it. quick checks: is this single-tenant or multi-tenant pool?
Maria (SRE): looks like SilverMast is on shared embeddings pool eu-west-1-pool-3 (quantized gpt-embed-3q). checking noisy neighbor signals and per-tenant token counts.
Alex (Oncall): can we correlate with recent large batch embeds? query: `sum by (tenant) (rate(requests_total{route="/v1/embeddings", pool="eu-west-1-pool-3"}[5m]))` — any tenant with big delta?
Maria (SRE): running that — found one tenant "ad-optimizer" with a spike ~09:05 producing ~1200 small-requests/s vs normal 40/s. their median size small but bursts caused queueing — tail amplification looks like p99->2.5s.
Kevin (Support): wow, customer reported same timeframe. SilverMast shared sample: ~8 concurrent requests per user, 50ms each, but high QPS from single IP.
Alex (Oncall): this smells like a noisy neighbor. mitigation options: 1) temporary per-tenant throttle on ad-optimizer, 2) move SilverMast to a less noisy pool, 3) apply allowlist / priority for SilverMast traffic.
Jenna (Customer Success): SilverMast wants fastest fix; prefer we avoid migrating them mid-day. can we do a per-tenant allowlist/priority instead?
Maria (SRE): we have two short-term levers: soft-throttle (rate limit to X rps) or tenant-priority which bumps SilverMast to higher queue weight. priority requires config deploy (~15m).
Alex (Oncall): let's do both: soft-throttle ad-optimizer to 75rps and enable priority for SilverMast in pool routing. I'll run commands.
Alex (Oncall): applying throttle rule: `POST /internal/tenants/ad-optimizer/throttle {"max_rps":75}` — response 200 OK.
Alex (Oncall): enabling tenant-priority for SilverMast: `PATCH /internal/pools/eu-west-1-pool-3/weights {"tenant":"silvermast","weight":100}` -> queued config deploy.
Oncall Bot: config deploy started for pool eu-west-1-pool-3 (deploy_id=cfg-8891)
Maria (SRE): observing metrics after throttle: within 90s p95 dropped from 420ms -> 210ms, p99 from 2.8s -> 360ms. error rate normalized.
Kevin (Support): relaying to SilverMast: "we applied mitigation, should be improved now — please confirm"
Jenna (Customer Success): customer confirms: search responds again, UI recovered. :white_check_mark: they asked for root cause analysis and permanent fix.
Alex (Oncall): next steps: 1) leave throttle in place for 2 hours while we validate, 2) schedule migration of ad-optimizer to dedicated embeddings-reserve-2, 3) follow-up RCA.
Maria (SRE): collected debug dump and KV-cache metrics, saving to /var/log/incidents/INC-1159-debug.gz. rough notes: no memory OOM, queue depth spiked to 120, kernel scheduling latency increased on that pool.
Alex (Oncall): ticketing: created internal task TASK-4521 to move ad-optimizer to reserved pool and review per-tenant fairshare smoothing. tagging eng-platform + infra.
Kevin (Support): SilverMast asked for allowlist to bypass soft-throttles for up to 5 minutes during flash bursts — is that safe?
Maria (SRE): we can create a temporary allowlist that gives priority tokens but better to tune fairshare. allowlist increases risk of prioritizing one customer; need CS sign-off.
Jenna (Customer Success): will ask SilverMast whether they want a permanent priority contract or prefer we provide a stricter noisy-tenant isolation.
Alex (Oncall): summarizing resolution: applied ad-optimizer throttle, enabled temporary priority for SilverMast, p99 back to acceptable range. monitoring for 1hr.
Oncall Bot: incident INC-1159 -> status: mitigated. auto-watchers notified.
Maria (SRE): follow-up actions to capture in RCA: 1) improve noisy-tenant detection alerting (detect spikes by tenant sooner), 2) auto-schedule short lived isolation (move offending tenant to reserve queue), 3) evaluate per-tenant burst credits to avoid similar amplification.
Alex (Oncall): marking thread resolved for now, will reopen if regressions observed. thanks all.
